summary: Turns the search page into a client component that reads q from the URL, fetches matching products and lists them under a results heading.

findings.title: Cross-site scripting through the search query in the heading
findings.problem: The heading injects the raw q URL parameter as HTML through dangerouslySetInnerHTML. Nothing sanitizes or escapes the query first.
findings.consequence: An attacker can send a crafted search link that runs script in the victim's session. The script can steal data or act as that user.
findings.fix: Render the query as a normal text child so React escapes it.

findings.title: Hooks called after a conditional early return
findings.problem: SearchPage returns early when q is missing, before it calls useState and useEffect. So the number of hooks changes between renders.
findings.consequence: React throws a rendered-more-hooks error when q goes from empty to set during client navigation. The page then crashes.
findings.fix: Call useState and useEffect before the early return. Inside the effect, skip the fetch when query is empty.

findings.title: Effect without a dependency array refetches forever
findings.problem: The effect has no dependency array, so it runs after every render. Each run stores a new results array, which triggers another render.
findings.consequence: The page sends search requests to the catalog API in an endless loop. This wastes the user's bandwidth and loads the server.
findings.fix: Pass a dependency array of [query] to useEffect.

findings.title: Search request failure is never handled
findings.problem: searchProducts throws when the response is not ok, and the effect chains only then with no catch. The rejected promise floats unhandled.
findings.consequence: A failed search raises an unhandled rejection, and the user sees an empty list with no error message.
findings.fix: Add a catch handler that records an error state and shows it to the user.

findings.title: List items rendered without a key
findings.problem: The results map returns li elements with no key prop. Product has a stable id field that could serve as the key.
findings.consequence: React warns in the console and reconciles list items poorly when results change.
findings.fix: Set key to product.id on each li.

findings.title: Search form removed with no replacement input
findings.problem: The change deletes the search form that submitted q. The empty state now asks users to type a search term but offers no input.
findings.consequence: Users who open the search page without q cannot start a search from it.
findings.fix: Keep the form with the q input on the page, at least in the empty state.

findings.title: New search page behaviour has no covering test
findings.problem: SearchPage now fetches and renders results and has a new empty-query branch. No test exercises any of this behaviour.
findings.consequence: Regressions like the fetch loop and the hook order crash can reach users undetected.
findings.fix: Add component tests for the empty query, a successful search and a failed search.
